question: Why is nuclear force called a short-range force? Give reason.

options.A: It is called short-range because it acts strongly at all distances, including atomic distances.
options.B: It is short-range because it exists only between protons and not between neutrons.
options.C: It is short-range because its strength increases continuously as separation becomes infinite.
options.D: Nuclear force is appreciable only when nucleons are separated by about a few femtometres ($\sim10^{-15}\,\text{m}$). At larger distances it rapidly becomes negligible, so it is called short-range.
